questions.q: In a Jupyter notebook, what is the kernel?
options: The file format the notebook is saved in
A menu for formatting Markdown cells
The running Python process that runs your cells and remembers every variable and import
The browser tab that displays the notebook
questions.explain: Every code cell is sent to the same kernel, which holds state such as variables and imports between cells.

questions.q: A cell contains the two lines total = 100 and then total * 2. What appears under the cell when you run it?
options: Nothing, because there is no print statement
200, the value of the last expression
100, the value of the first line
An error, because total is not defined yet
questions.explain: Jupyter displays the value of the last expression in a cell automatically, so print is not required.

questions.q: x is 10 in the kernel. A cell containing x = x * 2 followed by x is run twice. What is displayed after the second run?
options: An error, because a cell cannot be run twice
questions.explain: The first run makes x equal 20 in the kernel's memory; the second run doubles that to 40. This is hidden state.

questions.q: What is the best way to check that a notebook does not depend on hidden state?
options: Restart the kernel and run all cells from the top
questions.explain: Restarting wipes the kernel's memory; if every cell then runs cleanly in order, the notebook is self-contained.

questions.q: What does the number in brackets beside a code cell tell you?
options: How many lines the cell has
How many seconds the cell took
The order in which cells were actually executed
questions.explain: The execution count shows run order. Jumbled numbers are a warning that the notebook may not read top to bottom.
